status: explicit approximation from published dimensions; not an author-faithful apparatus reproduction
assumptions: The SmCo5 core is a uniformly polarized cylinder with radius and half-height 1.25 mm.
The cylinder axis and source spin are along y, while its center lies 50 mm from the sensor along x.
The measured harmonic is the y component of the pseudomagnetic field at transverse source orientation.
The 12 mm spherical sensor cell has uniform response weighting.
The soft-iron contribution to the stated total source spin is not spatially modeled.
Shielding changes ordinary magnetic leakage but not the exotic tensor-Yukawa field.

method.sourceCore: deterministic Gauss-Legendre quadrature over cylinder axial coordinate and squared radius, with periodic angular quadrature
method.sensorCell: exact uniform-ball mean-value factor for a source-free modified-Helmholtz field: 3*(z*cosh(z)-sinh(z))/z^3, z=R_cell/lambda
method.normalization: response divided by the transverse center-point kernel at the same center distance and force range

findings.reportedSevenMillimetreRange: The uniform-core correction is +0.326 percent, the uniform-cell factor is +7.542 percent, and the combined factor is 1.07893.
findings.shortRange: At 2 mm the combined response is 2.34881 times the center-point estimate because the cell radius is three force ranges and nearer detector volume is exponentially favored.
findings.dominantFiniteSizeAtSevenMillimetres: Under the declared assumptions, sensor-volume averaging dominates the SmCo5-core correction.
findings.likelihoodImpact: Because the inferred coupling product is inversely proportional to modeled response, omitting the 7 mm combined correction would shift the approximate coupling scale downward by about 7.32 percent when corrected.
findings.limit: The result cannot reproduce the publication's limit until the combined SmCo5/soft-iron spin density, sensor polarization weighting, exact coordinate convention and likelihood are supplied.
